messages:
Sam (CS): Hey team — putting together an exec-friendly follow-up email for ACME about yesterday's embeddings throughput incident. Draft below. Need engineering timeline + confirmation of mitigations, and support + legal OK on credit wording.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 2479123001 — embeddings-throughput-drop — P1 — pages sent to @Jordan (SRE) at 2026-03-14T22:04:12Z. Status: RESOLVED 2026-03-14T22:37:58Z. Alerts: 7x GPU saturation, autoscaler thrash.

Jordan (SRE): Timeline and quick notes below. TL;DR: transient autoscaler loop + degraded KV cache eviction under heavy prefix reuse. We mitigated by pinning model variant and ramping pool to reserved nodes.

Jordan (SRE): ```
22:03:41Z - monitoring detected 5x latency spikes on embeddings-prod
22:04:10Z - paging triggered, on-call notified (Jordan)
22:06:22Z - initial investigation: sudden queue growth on pool-emb-1
22:08:05Z - observed autoscaler creating then tearing down 2 nodes repeatedly
22:15:33Z - rule applied: disable aggressive burst scale for pool-emb-1
22:20:12Z - pinned to model-emb-v2-int8 to avoid kernel fallback path
22:37:58Z - queues drained, latency returned to baseline
Root cause: autoscaler policy + kernel fallback triggered by cold KV cache churn.
Workaround: pin variant + temporarily disable burst scaler.
Permanent fix: change autoscaler hysteresis + improve KV cache warmup footprint.
```

Mike (Eng): Confirming Jordan's root cause. Follow-ups planned:
- Change autoscaler cooldown from 30s -> 4m for embedding pools.
- Add pre-warm job for KV cache on new node attach (batch preload).
- Add metric to track kernel-fallback-rate so we can alert earlier.
ETA for fixes: autoscaler policy change + metric: 2 days (staged rollout). KV pre-warm: 1 week.

Priya (Product): For customer messaging, we should avoid deep infra terms. High-level phrasing: 'brief autoscaling behavior during a transient workload spike caused a temporary slowdown; we've implemented immediate mitigations and are rolling out safeguards to prevent recurrence.' Engineers, can we provide a short 2-line non-technical description?

Mike (Eng): Two-line non-tech: 'An automated scaling interaction during a sudden spike briefly increased request latency for embeddings. We applied a targeted mitigation to stabilize capacity and are deploying safeguards to prevent similar disruptions.'

Elaine (Support): Suggest we offer ACME a credit equivalent to 10% of last month's embeddings spend for the 33-minute impact window; legal confirmed that's within our standard SLO credit table. Also recommend offering a 30-minute walkthrough with our SRE lead to review what changed and how we prevent it.

acme_ops: Thanks, Sam. We appreciate the quick fix. We're most concerned about recurrence and whether any data/requests were dropped or misrouted. Can you confirm there was no data loss?

Jordan (SRE): No data loss. All in-flight requests either retried successfully by the client or completed during remediation. We have tracebacks for all affected requests — happy to provide sanitized examples.

Sam (CS): Draft email for ACME (please review/edit):

```
Subject: Follow-up: Embeddings latency incident on 2026-03-14

Hi Team,

Thanks again for your patience during yesterday's disruption. Summary: between 22:03 and 22:38 UTC we experienced a partial degradation of the embeddings service which increased latency for a subset of requests.

What happened (short): An automated scaling interaction during a sudden workload spike caused transient capacity instability. Our team applied targeted mitigations to stabilize capacity and routed traffic to a tested model variant.

Impact: Some requests experienced elevated latency for ~33 minutes. There was no data loss and no incorrect outputs.

What we did: Pinned model variant, disabled aggressive burst scaling for the affected pool, and drained queues.

Next steps (what we will do for you):
- Implement autoscaler cooldown increases and add a pre-warm job for node attach (ETA: 1 week).
- Add a new metric to detect kernel fallback events earlier (ETA: 48 hours).
- Offer a 30-minute SRE walkthrough and a one-time account credit covering the impacted window.

We apologize for the disruption. If you want the detailed engineering timeline or sanitized traces, we can share them.

Best,
Sam (Customer Success)
```

Priya (Product): This reads well. For exec audience add a single 'what we changed now' bullet at the top.

Sam (CS): Added short 'what we changed now' line at top of email.

Elaine (Support): Once we sign off, I'll send with a scheduling link for the SRE walkthrough and include the credit statement. Suggested credit sentence: 'We will apply a one-time account credit equivalent to 10% of your embeddings usage for the billing period to reflect the impacted window.' Legal OK?

Mike (Eng): Legal fine. Just note: credit language should not be seen as admission of broader SLA breach beyond the window. Elaine's wording looks good.

Jordan (SRE): Quick internal handoff log for on-call continuity (for the record):
- Paged: Jordan at 22:04:12Z (pager duty)
- Secondary: Mike alerted at 22:08:30Z
- Escalation to Eng lead: 22:12:02Z (Priya looped in)
- On-call change: Jordan handed off to Mike for post-incident followups at 23:05:00Z.

Sam (CS): Final checklist before sending to ACME:
1) Engineering timeline + sanitized traces attached -> Jordan to confirm by 2479123600.
2) Credit amount + billing team notification -> Elaine to confirm by 2479123650.
3) Executive note / single-sentence summary -> Priya to sign off.
4) Send -> Sam (CS) will send once all confirm.

Jordan (SRE): Timeline + sanitized traces attached to this thread (link: https://redwood.internal/trace/2479123001) — please redact customer PII. Confirmed by me.

Elaine (Support): Billing notified, credit approved at 2479123695, ACME billing contact cc list confirmed. I'll draft the email header and schedule the walkthrough.

acme_ops: Appreciate the updates. We'll take the walkthrough and want to understand if any of our usage patterns triggered the scaling behavior — happy to share recent load patterns with your SRE.

Sam (CS): Great. Last item: public status page update we posted during the incident — here's the refined post-mortem blurb for status.redwood.com (short):

"Between 22:03 and 22:38 UTC on 2026-03-14, customers using the embeddings endpoint experienced elevated latency due to an automated scaling interaction during a sudden traffic spike. Mitigations were applied and full service restored. We are deploying autoscaler and cache warmup safeguards to prevent recurrence."

Priya (Product): Nice — concise, non-technical. :thumbsup:

Sam (CS): OK team — if everyone confirms the attachments (Jordan) and billing credit (Elaine), I'll send the customer-facing email in ~15 minutes and post the finalized snippet to the status page. Marking thread for follow-up: last_message_ts 2479123740. :eyes:

incident-bot: Note: channel reminder set for 2479200000 to verify fix rollout metrics and confirm closure of engineering tasks.

Mike (Eng): Confirmed — autoscaler policy change will be in canary tomorrow morning. I'll post the PR link when created.

Sam (CS): Sending now. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
